object_description: two dark buildings with rounded corners and staggered heights, each formed of interlocking rectangular volumes
design_condition: the two buildings mark both the end and the beginning of the street and define the transition to the village centre, opened and accessible on all four sides so the site reads as public space

positive: Precise positioning with continuous public use on the ground floor creates a place of high social and cultural diversity
Opening and accessibility on all four sides makes the site consciously perceived as public space in the district
The ensemble complements the neighbouring park and clinic in a comprehensible way, like a string of pearls
The intersecting rectangular volumes give a beautifully proportioned residential building that fits typologically along the street
The core with lift, staircase and wet rooms leaves a flexible spatial layer that can be used efficiently and to a high standard
The lower part of the hall building takes up the scale of the neighbouring courtyard building as a foyer open on three sides
The external appearance of the hall is simple but precisely designed
Two-storey continuous wooden pilaster strips hint at the festival hall and its significance for the community
The openings let the hall look outwards and enter into a dialogue with the public space
The continuously sloping square follows the terrain without requiring walls or stairs
Simple clear orientation and equivalent entrance situations create a strong potential for identity
The floor plan structure is flexible in room separation, use and apartment sizes
The hybrid construction and materialisation allow economical construction and reasonable operating and maintenance costs
The simple static design with prefabricated timber and a concrete skeleton means low investment costs
The work balances sustainable aspects with social participation, appropriate scale, Minergie standard and renewable materials
negative: The interpretation of the site as a continuous public space must be critically questioned
The interior concept of foyer and hall is neither atmospherically nor constructively convincing
The interior reads as a multi-purpose hall rather than a space dedicated to art and culture
The concept lacks a differentiated formulation of the various connections to the surroundings
The pergola in front of the foyer does not take the existing infrastructure into account and does not support the quality of stay in the courtyard outside events
The bicycle parking spaces are not feasible due to the existing staircase
The location of the kitchen is controversial
The location and height of the storage space planned as an extension of the hall is not convincing
The route to the visitor toilets is awkward and unclear
Only two-thirds of the permitted use is utilised, so economic efficiency is unlikely to be outstanding
In terms of economical use of land resources the project is rated below average
The identity-creating power of the hall building still needs to be clarified and strengthened, especially inside
